```{r}
# ---- Improved Correlation Matrix Visualization ----
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(corrplot)
library(RColorBrewer)

# ---- 1. Load Data ----
# Replace with your actual data loading code
analysis_data <- read.csv("~/Documents/GitHub/h1b-econ-paper/improved_processed_data_for_analysis_April1st.csv")

# Fix numeric versions of binary variables for correlation analysis
analysis_data$high_dependency_median_num <- as.numeric(analysis_data$high_dependency_median)
analysis_data$post_treatment_num <- as.numeric(analysis_data$post_treatment)
analysis_data$did_median_num <- as.numeric(analysis_data$did_median)

# Create period indicator for pre/post policy
analysis_data$period <- factor(ifelse(analysis_data$year < 2017, 
                                     "Pre-Policy (2012-2016)", 
                                     "Post-Policy (2017-2020)"),
                              levels = c("Pre-Policy (2012-2016)", "Post-Policy (2017-2020)"))

# ---- 2. Create Correlation Matrices ----
# Key variables for correlation matrix (using numeric versions of binary variables)
cor_vars <- c("log_real_wage", "denial_rate", "avg_preperiod_dependency", 
              "high_dependency_median_num", "post_treatment_num", "did_median_num",
              "total_approvals", "total_denials")

# Create correlation matrix for all data
cor_matrix <- cor(analysis_data[, cor_vars], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# For period-specific correlations
pre_data <- analysis_data %>% filter(period == "Pre-Policy (2012-2016)")
post_data <- analysis_data %>% filter(period == "Post-Policy (2017-2020)")

# Variables with non-zero variance in pre-period
pre_cor_vars <- c("log_real_wage", "denial_rate", "avg_preperiod_dependency", 
                 "high_dependency_median_num", "total_approvals", "total_denials")
pre_cor <- cor(pre_data[, pre_cor_vars], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Variables with non-zero variance in post-period
post_cor_vars <- c("log_real_wage", "denial_rate", "avg_preperiod_dependency", 
                  "high_dependency_median_num", "did_median_num", 
                  "total_approvals", "total_denials")
post_cor <- cor(post_data[, post_cor_vars], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# ---- 3. Improved Visualization with Better Readability ----
# Define a better color palette
col_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("#6BAED6", "#FFFFFF", "#E6550D"))(100)

# Create a PDF with better formatting
pdf("improved_correlation_matrices.pdf", width = 12, height = 15)
par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))

# Function to create improved correlation plot
create_improved_corrplot <- function(cor_data, title) {
  corrplot(cor_data, 
           method = "color",           # Use color fill
           type = "upper",             # Show only upper triangle
           order = "original",         # Keep original variable order
           col = col_palette,          # Use our custom palette
           addCoef.col = "black",      # White text for dark cells
           tl.col = "black",           # Black text for variable names
           tl.srt = 45,                # Rotate text labels
           tl.cex = 0.9,               # Slightly smaller text for labels
           cl.cex = 0.9,               # Slightly smaller text for legend
           diag = FALSE,               # No diagonal
           title = title,              # Add title
           mar = c(0, 0, 3, 0),        # Margins
           bg = "white",               # White background
           outline = TRUE,             # Add outline
           addgrid.col = "lightgray",  # Light grid color
           # Add a callback function to dynamically color coefficients
           number.cex = 0.9,           # Slightly smaller coefficient text
           number.digits = 2,          # Show only 2 decimal places 
           addCoefasPercent = FALSE)   # Show as coefficients, not percentages
  
  # # Add rectangle around the plot for better definition
  # box("figure", col = "black", lwd = 2)
}

# Main correlation matrix
create_improved_corrplot(cor_matrix, "All Data (2012-2020)")

# Pre-policy correlation
create_improved_corrplot(pre_cor, "Pre-Policy (2012-2016)")

# Post-policy correlation
create_improved_corrplot(post_cor, "Post-Policy (2017-2020)")

dev.off()

# ---- 4. Create Interactive HTML Version (More Readable) ----
# If you have htmlwidgets and plotly installed
if(require(plotly) && require(reshape2)) {
  # Convert correlation matrices to long format for plotly
  cor_matrix_long <- melt(cor_matrix)
  names(cor_matrix_long) <- c("Var1", "Var2", "value")
  
  # Create interactive heatmap
  p <- plot_ly(
    data = cor_matrix_long,
    x = ~Var1,
    y = ~Var2,
    z = ~value,
    type = "heatmap",
    colorscale = list(c(0, "#6BAED6"), c(0.5, "#FFFFFF"), c(1, "#E6550D")),
    text = ~paste0("r = ", round(value, 2)),
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) %>%
    layout(
      title = "Interactive Correlation Matrix (All Data)",
      xaxis = list(title = ""),
      yaxis = list(title = "")
    )
  
  # Save as HTML
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(p, "interactive_correlation_matrix.html")
}

# ---- 5. Create PNG Version with Better Background Contrast ----
# For better default viewing in documents
png("improved_correlation_matrices_horizontal.png", width = 2000, height = 667, res = 150)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))

# Use the same function to create better correlation plots
create_improved_corrplot(cor_matrix, "All Data (2012-2020)")
create_improved_corrplot(pre_cor, "Pre-Policy (2012-2016)")
create_improved_corrplot(post_cor, "Post-Policy (2017-2020)")

dev.off()

# Print confirmation
cat("Improved correlation matrices created with better readability.\n")
```
